Fix review: blocked 69a429cfab2d02fd938ac13ef2893c520ca98f7a mutant-survived: an explicit roster ref is silently replaced by the default, and the CLI group path's --head and --roster-ref pass-through are unpinned

bus-nonce: e26587b46a7a1e4b238a4d699abd2d06

Round 2 re-review (third pass over this group: round 1 blocked at 6684dee65, this is the fixer's round 2 plus a main merge). Measured at 69a429cfab2d02fd938ac13ef2893c520ca98f7a in a detached worktree. The merge base equals origin/main 1ebc737e7, and roles/ has not changed between them. Spec: the pack file R10-FLOW-DISPATCH.json at 30c57744a. Roster: origin/handoff/audit-r10-roster at 545184b96.

## Block

Round 1 blocked on the head-ignored mutant: an explicit `head` replaced by a ref's tip while 42 checks stayed green. Round 2 pinned that one argument but left the same class open on the other explicit source the round added. With the mutant `roster_ref = roster_lib.reader_ref(repo_dir, roster_ref)` -> `roster_lib.reader_ref(repo_dir, None)`, all 48 self-test checks pass. In a fixture where origin/main and the round roster branch carry different briefs, `dispatch_group(..., roster_ref="origin/main")` then publishes the round branch's brief instead of main's (ev/explicit_roster_ref_demo.txt: unmutated `MAIN`, mutant `BRANCH`). That is a silently wrong brief on the documented `--roster-ref REF` interface. The CLI `--group` path, which is the operator's entry point and prints the line a standing trigger is fired with, is not called by any check. Dropping its `--head` (`head=args.head or ""` -> `head=""`) or its `--roster-ref` (`roster_ref=args.roster_ref` -> `None`) also leaves 48/48 green. For a fixer, the dropped `--head` silently dispatches at main's tip. A mutant drive that pins only the named lines, while its sibling inputs on the same path stay unpinned, does not meet fixer.md's mutation proof. The cost is two or three checks in `_group_checks`: an explicit `roster_ref` reading the other roster's brief, and one `main(["--group", ...])` call with `--head` and `--roster-ref` asserting both reach the prompt.

## Findings

- Unpinned: `dispatch_group`'s explicit `roster_ref` (mutant explicit-roster-ref-ignored, failed=0). The demo shows the wrong brief is published. Evidence: ev/reviewer_mutants_head.txt, ev/explicit_roster_ref_demo.txt. Carry: dismissed: returned to the fixer in this blocked verdict (item 61800936)
- Unpinned: the CLI `--group` path's pass-through of `--head` and `--roster-ref` (mutants cli-head-dropped and cli-roster-ref-dropped, failed=0 each). No check invokes `main` with `--group`. Carry: dismissed: returned to the fixer in this blocked verdict (item 83f73eb7)
- Unpinned, lower weight: `_publish`'s fetch of an existing dispatch ref (mutant fetch-skipped, failed=0). It survives because the fixture dispatches from the clone that made the earlier commit, so the tip object is already local. From a second clone the `rev-parse <tip>^{tree}` refuses, which fails loudly rather than silently. A second-clone re-dispatch check would pin it. Carry: dismissed: returned to the fixer in this blocked verdict (item 695058e1)
- Near-equivalent mutant: running `_publish`'s `ref_privacy.refusal` on a constant ref instead of `ref` survives, because the commit message `dispatch: {ref}` carries the same home path and the message check catches it. Only the ref-only `_REF_CHARS` rule goes unexercised, and git's own ref-name check stands behind it. The brief's `if why` pin (privacy-off) is killed. Carry: dismissed: home-path case caught by the message check (item bd9a4d57)
- Body figure stale at this head: the body's `cloud_dispatch self-test: 46 checks, 0 failed` was measured at the code head 742ed664. At 69a429cf it prints 48 checks, 0 failed. Both added checks come from main (#2583's carry-section prompt checks; main 1ebc737e7 alone prints 32). Re-measured: 742ed664 prints 46. Carry: dismissed: main merge adds two checks (item 15632c35)
- The roster carry for the deferred arm (R10-FLOW-MAIN-GATE, item b87aa9e4, at 545184b96) names the behaviour but no control, unlike the K17 carry's `Control:` clause (finding-propagation.md, "carry the control, not only the claim"). It also says "must land before #2577 review", which contradicts the deferral the orchestrator ruled under mandate 6319294694. Suggested control: a reviewer dispatch at a head whose required context's latest run concluded failure refuses and pushes nothing, and the same head with that run green renders. Carry: R10-FLOW-MAIN-GATE (item 1fb1501b)

## Evidence

- The deferral is disclosed: the body states the revision-7 reviewer refusal arm is not built, says why (R10-FLOW-MAIN-GATE's classifier is not on origin/main; building it on the check-runs API would duplicate that concept, fixer.md step 17), says `dispatch_group("reviewer", ...)` still renders for any head, and carries it as `Carry: R10-FLOW-MAIN-GATE (item b87aa9e4)`. That item is on the roster branch, and 58bf922e is its ancestor. Judged as the orchestrator directed: the disclosure is adequate. The carry text is the subject of the last finding above.
- The K17 seam carry (item 92bca45d) is on R10-ORCH-MACHINERY at the roster branch, and 903d137b is its ancestor. It now names both the bus.sh `dispatch` reviewer-fire close and the worker registry, and states `Control: a dispatch through dispatch_group leaves a reviewer-fire close in the ledger`. This settles round 1's workers.json item.
- Roster-ref and head separation pin: the check "by default the brief is the round's roster branch's and the head is main's tip, not that branch's" fails under roster-ref-main and head-from-roster-ref (failed=1 each). Its fixture puts the roster branch one commit ahead of main with its own brief. Confirmed.
- Survivor pins: head-ignored failed=1 and privacy-off failed=1, both killed. Confirmed.
- Brief-drop figure: failed=5 at this head, naming the five checks the body lists. Confirmed.
- The fixer's drive at this head (ev/fixer_drive_head.txt): M0 failed=0 null-ok; `RESULT mutants=13 survived=0`. Every per-mutant figure matches the body: tree-skip 2, brief-drop 5, nonce-altered 1, prompt-wrong 4, render-host-off 5, reviewer-head-off 1, roster-ref-main 1, head-from-roster-ref 1. topic-to-id, parent-drop and roster-repo-ignored all CRASHED (failed=-1).
- My own drive (ev/mydrive.py, ev/reviewer_mutants_head.txt): 10 mutants, 7 survived. Three of the survivors are judged equivalent: flagpath-head-required-off (render refuses a non-hex head, exit 2, demonstrated), cli-model-check-off (render refuses a missing model, its own check), and privacy-checks-message-only. The other four are the findings above. reviewer-guard-any-role and group-missing-no-refuse CRASHED (killed), and head-ignored-reviewer-only was killed by a named check.
- Figures re-derived at this head (ev/figures.txt): `MODE: SCOPED -- 1 script(s) run` (6 changed files); entities `ALL 2382 ENTITY CHECKS PASSED`; `STRUCTURE RATCHET PASSED`; `Architecture score: dS +0.0000 NULL`; ref_privacy 0 refused (cloud_dispatch.py GUARDED); tmp_paths 0 refused; throwaway_git 0 refused; `ALL 109 HARNESS HEADER CHECKS PASSED`; `claims hygiene: origin/main ok`. Class grep (ev/class_grep.txt): empty at the head, and two `MAIN_REF` defaults at 6684dee65, as the body says.
- VERSION, the manifest, RELEASE_NOTES.md, tests/golden and the claim files are untouched in the three-dot diff. ref_privacy.py is outside the group's `files` but is required, because the module now pushes and its PUSHERS entry must say GUARDED.
- `git merge-tree --write-tree origin/main 69a429cf` exits 0, tree 1d399250b (ev/merge_tree.txt).
- CI at this head (check-runs API, 46 runs): the only red is nightly-status, which grades main and is answered in the body's `## Red checks`. pr-contract succeeded (21:16:34Z, and 21:20:17Z on the body edit). mutation is green, but it draws no mutant from tools/ lines. `closures` (job 119502008639) was still in progress when this verdict was written, so its conclusion is not part of this review.
- The head was re-read from ls-remote before writing: refs/heads/fix/r10-flow-dispatch is still 69a429cfab2d02fd938ac13ef2893c520ca98f7a.

RESULT fixer-drive: mutants=13 survived=0 (M0 null-ok)
RESULT reviewer-drive: mutants=10 survived=7, of which equivalent=3 and real=4
RESULT selftest: 48 checks, 0 failed (body: 46 at the code head)
- `carry_audit.py --roster-ref origin/handoff/audit-r10-roster check`, with this verdict passed as a comment: `CARRY-AUDIT: 1 finding item(s): 1 routed, 0 unrouted, 0 bad destination(s)` (ev/carry_audit.txt).

RESULT merge-tree: clean
RESULT ci: 1 red (nightly-status, main's), answered; closures pending

This is round 5. Rounds 1 to 4 blocked, the last at 1060a1f035db0bb84263080ec4b36343a742c870 with class-open (the `--group` CLI accepted `--env-id`, `--brief`, `--topic`, `--repo` and `--out`, dropped them, and exited 0). I measured at 9720cda1ebc3cb8304e62b5914910d54642e721a in detached worktrees. I followed fix-review.md as it stands on origin/main 3976515a0. The roles/ diff from the merge base 93e6a63d2 to main is non-empty only in wording, where the block-class spellings changed (`class-open: <seam>`), so I used main's copy. Roster: origin/handoff/audit-r10-roster at 306a96d5f. The finder's harness is the round-4 reviewer's demo and drive from origin/review/2577 (ea561e6ca): demo_dropped_flags.py (sha1 affe53b68) and mydrive_r4.py (sha1 27bf92597). I also re-ran the round-3 drive (sha1 b30194ef7).

## Findings

- The round-4 roster carry item (2), the hot-file reviewer refusal arm (refuse a reviewer at a head that shares pr_args.sh, update_pr.sh, cloud_relay.sh, orchestrator_tick.py or r10_seat_selftests_mutants.py with an open pull request holding an unboarded merge verdict), is now deferred in the body to R10-FLOW-MAIN-GATE, beside arm (a). Its routing is valid: carry_audit reports 0 unrouted, and R10-FLOW-MAIN-GATE is live at stage not-started. But that group's roster `carry` at 306a96d5f holds only arm (a), as item b87aa9e4, with its control. Arm (b) is not on it yet, and the body states no control for (b). Before the merge it has to be written into R10-FLOW-MAIN-GATE's roster carry with a control. A suitable control: a reviewer dispatch at a head sharing a hot file with an open PR that holds an unboarded merge verdict refuses, and the same dispatch with the verdict boarded passes. Carry: R10-FLOW-MAIN-GATE
- Surviving mutant refusal-truthy: `getattr(args, dest) != ap.get_default(dest)` -> `getattr(args, dest)`, failed=0. It is equivalent on every live input. It differs only for an explicitly empty value (`--brief ""`, `--env-id ""` and so on), and the flag path also reads an empty value as "absent" (`if args.brief`), so no seat changes. Carry: dismissed: equivalent, an empty flag is a no-op on both paths
- Surviving mutants refusal-skip-first (the loop skips GROUP_FLAGS' first entry, `role`, whose disposition is forwarded) and flag-checks-unrun (deletes the `_flag_checks(check)` call, a test deletion, not a production change), failed=0 each. The first is equivalent by construction (skipping a `None` entry refuses nothing), and the second is not a production mutant. Carry: dismissed: equivalent or not a production mutant
- Surviving mutant model-check-off (failed=0, also a survivor at 1060a1f). It is equivalent because render refuses a missing model, as the body already says. Carry: dismissed: equivalent, the refusal is render's own

## Evidence

- Round-4 blocks, each cleared at this head:
  - Class-open, five dropped flags: cleared. The finder's demo at 1060a1f prints `rc 0 stdout dispatch/x` with all five values DROPPED (ev/demo_prev.txt). At the head it prints `cloud_dispatch: refused: --topic does not apply with --group: ...`, `rc 2 stdout ` (empty), `forwarded []` (ev/demo_wt.txt). The demo's DROPPED lines at the head are vacuous, because nothing was dispatched. The per-flag exit-2 behaviour is pinned by the five `--group refuses --<flag>` checks, all red under refusal-warn-only (my drive) and under group-refusal-off (the fixer's drive, failed=5).
  - Roster carry item (2): dispositioned in the body (deferred with a Carry); the roster state is the first Finding.
  - Round history restated in the body: cleared. The body cites the round-4 harnesses only as the finder's harness at both ends.
  - pr-truncated-1: cleared. Finder drive mydrive_r4: at 1060a1f `RESULT mutants=9 survived=1` (pr-truncated-1 failed=0, ev/mydrive_r4_prev.txt); at the head `RESULT mutants=9 survived=0`, pr-truncated-1 failed=2 (ev/mydrive_r4_head.txt). M0 is null-ok at both ends, and pr-none and nonce-none are CRASHED at both, as the body says. The body's figures are re-derived.
- Round-3 drive at the head (ev/finder_r3_head.txt): `RESULT mutants=6 survived=0`.
- Mutation proof, my own drive (reviewer-built, ev/mydrive_r5.py, disclosed as mine): 25 one-occurrence mutants over every pass-through `main()` forwards to `dispatch_group`, plus the refusal arm and GROUP_FLAGS, plus the flag-checks deletion as a control, for 26 in all. Pass-throughs mutated: role (constant fixer, constant reviewer), group, model, roster_ref (None), head (empty), head/roster_ref swapped, pr (empty, last char), nonce (empty, first 3), pr/nonce swapped, overlay (None). Every one is killed. Refusal arm: refusal-warn-only killed (failed=5), refusal-skip-last killed (failed=1, `--out`). Each refused flag flipped to forwarded (topic, brief, repo, out) is killed by its own `--group forwards` check. A deleted brief entry is killed by the table check, and pr/overlay flipped to refused are killed by the fixture checks. Head: M0 null-ok, `RESULT mutants=26 survived=4`, with the 4 survivors listed under Findings (ev/mydrive_r5_head.txt). Null control at 1060a1f (ev/mydrive_r5_prev.txt): the pass-through mutants that apply survive more often there (model-const and pr-suffix-1 survive), and the table mutants do not apply. So the new `_flag_checks` accounts for the added kills.
- Sibling flags: I found none the class misses. The parser's actions less help are 13. The body's rule prints 13 seams, 8 forwarded and 5 refused, none UNLISTED (ev/seam_rule.txt). Null control: a copy with `--extra` added prints `extra UNLISTED`. argparse prefix abbreviations resolve to the same dests. The group path's only other inputs are `os.environ` (cloud_dispatch.py:270, 284, the documented environment source) and `--self-test` (an exact-argv short-circuit, not a parser flag) (ev/other_inputs.txt). The body states the enumeration rule.
- Fixer's drive at the head (ev/fixer_drive_head.txt): M0 null-ok, `RESULT mutants=27 survived=0`. parent-drop, topic-to-id and roster-repo-ignored are CRASHED. Re-derived, and it matches the body's per-mutant counts (group-refusal-off 5, env-id-forwarded-as-none 1, flag-unlisted 2, cli-pr-truncated 2).
- Self-test: 66 checks, 0 failed at the head (ev/selftest_head.txt) and 52 at 1060a1f (ev/selftest_prev.txt). Re-derived (+14 = 1 table check + 13 flags).
- Figures (ev/figures.txt), all re-derived and matching the body: `MODE: SCOPED -- 1 script(s) run, 32 scoped out.` (6 changed files); `ALL 109 HARNESS HEADER CHECKS PASSED`; `claims hygiene: origin/main ok`; `ALL 124 closure shrink pins PASSED`; `layout self-test: ok`; `STRUCTURE RATCHET PASSED`; `Architecture score: dS +0.0000 NULL`; ref_privacy `0 refused`; tmp_paths `0 refused`; throwaway_git `0 raw git init or clone site(s) refused`; `CI PREDICT: no closures or fast red predicted`; three-dot stat `6 files changed, 495 insertions(+), 18 deletions(-)`. VERSION, the manifest, RELEASE_NOTES.md, the goldens and the claim files are untouched (0 lines), so no env_drift claim is owed.
- I did not re-run `ALL 2382 ENTITY CHECKS PASSED` (the scoped gate's heavy script). Per step 11 I cite CI instead: `fast (3.14)` concluded success at this head.
- Head (ev/head_topology.txt): 9720cda1e = merge(1060a1f03, 9dcdfe948). 9dcdfe948 -> e96aaeff2 -> fe6080b3e = merge(1060a1f03, origin/main 93e6a63d2). This matches the body's Head section. `refs/heads/fix/r10-flow-dispatch` is 9720cda1ebc3cb8304e62b5914910d54642e721a at write time.
- Merge: `git merge-tree --write-tree origin/main 9720cda1ebc3cb8304e62b5914910d54642e721a` against origin/main 3976515a0 gives rc=0, tree edd5fc673 (ev/merge_tree.txt). The head is clean, so no absorb is owed.
- Red checks (ev/checkruns.tsv, check-runs API per commit): 41 runs at the head. The one failure is nightly-status, which grades main, and the body answers it. pr-contract succeeded twice (02:00:30Z, 02:01:07Z), and closure-scope, scope and mutation succeeded. The body routes main's ci-ratchet red to its owner, and ci-ratchet is skipped here. fe6080b3e, e96aaeff2 and 9dcdfe948 carry no runs, as the body says. Final re-read once every workflow concluded (ev/checkruns_final.tsv): 49 runs, 32 success, 16 skipped, 1 failure (nightly-status); coverage, fast (3.14) and Analyze (python) concluded success.
- Body carry audit (ev/carry_audit_body.txt): `CARRY-AUDIT: 1 finding item(s): 1 routed, 0 unrouted, 0 bad destination(s)`. This verdict's Carry destination, R10-FLOW-MAIN-GATE, is live at stage not-started (ev/main_gate_entry.json).
- Architecture (step 15): the parser moves into `_parser()`, so one parser serves main() and the self-test. GROUP_FLAGS is a single table that owns each flag's disposition, and the refusal raises Refusal on the existing exit-2 path. I found no breach.
- The worktrees were clean after every drive (ev/worktrees_clean.txt).
